title: Strings, bytes and runes
summary: UTF-8 under the hood: why len is not the number of characters, and how to process text safely.
hints: `RuneCount`: `for range s { n++ }` already counts runes, because `range` over a string steps one *code point* at a time (and yields `utf8.RuneError` for invalid bytes). `ReverseString`: convert with `r := []rune(s)`, swap from both ends, and convert back with `string(r)`.

`IsPalindrome`: build a `[]rune` holding only the letters and digits (`unicode.IsLetter`, `unicode.IsDigit`), lower-cased with `unicode.ToLower`, then compare it with its reverse by walking two indices inward. `TruncateRunes`: loop `for i := range s` (i is the *byte* offset of each rune) counting runes, and when you have seen `n` of them return `s[:i]`; if the loop ends first, return `s`.

`CaesarShift`: work rune by rune. For `'a' <= r && r <= 'z'` compute `'a' + (r-'a'+shift)%26` where `shift` is `((k % 26) + 26) % 26` so negative `k` works; same for upper case; anything else (spaces, punctuation, accented letters) is copied unchanged. Collect into a `strings.Builder` or a `[]rune`.
